label: Coexistence
blurb: People and nature together: how much of the basin's wetland is protected or conserved, the benefits nature provides to people, and population pressure.

method: Protected or conserved share is the share of the basin's wetland area in res-8 cells inside any WDPA protected area (excluding 'Proposed') or WD-OECM other effective conservation measure (May 2026); distinct cells, since areas overlap. This is designated, not effective, protection, and it includes Ramsar Sites that are listed in the WDPA. Nature's contributions to people is the area-weighted mean count of contributions a location ranks highly for in Chaplin-Kramer et al. (2019), 0–19; it counts as a benefit, so higher ranks higher. Population density is GHS-POP 2020 over the basin area; more people per km² ranks lower. Whether population should count as pressure is a team decision. Basins are HydroBASINS v1c polygons as H3 res-6 cells (~36 km²): level-6 basins are filled by cell centre and coarser levels are unions of level-6 basins by Pfafstetter code. Wetland is GLWD v2 classes 8–32 (lacustrine, riverine, palustrine, ephemeral, peatland and coastal wetlands); open water and rice paddies are left out. Scores are mid-rank percentiles (0–100) among the basins at the chosen level, with direction applied so higher is better for the pillar; tied values share the midpoint of their rank range. The pillar score is the plain mean of the variable percentiles. All of this is provisional: which variables belong to which pillar, and how they are weighted, has not been decided.
